0.title: Head Up
0.quote: I don't need a perfect wing. I need enough clarity to see the next right movement, and enough courage to extend my wings into it.

1.title: Spiritual Life
1.quote: You can only renegotiate with air you're willing to see.
1.air_intro: Your relationship with whatever is larger than you, however you name it, and what it gives your life: meaning, direction, a place to rest. Any faith or none.
1.air_q1: When do I feel most connected to something larger than me?
1.air_q2: When do I feel furthest away?
beliefs: I have to earn my place.
Doubt means I'm doing it wrong.
My spiritual life is private, so I don't need anyone.
I'm too busy for this right now.
I'm held, even when I can't feel it.
There's a purpose in my being here.
1.horizon_intro: Picture an ordinary day a year from now. How do you begin it? Where do you find stillness? How do you meet a hard moment? Who shares this part of life with you? What do you give back?
flight: stillness, prayer, gratitude, reading, nature, music, whatever connects you
what I'll protect, and what I'll say no to
1.soul_intro: Once a day for seven days, stop for two minutes and ask: where is the lift in this moment? A kindness, some beauty, a feeling of being held, a breath that finally slowed. Write one line.
1.gathering: What did Find the Lift show you?

2.title: Character
2.quote: Character is who you are when no one's watching, and who you're becoming, one choice at a time.
2.air_intro: Clear sight, not self-punishment. How closely do my everyday actions match what I say matters to me?
2.air_words: Three words the people closest to me would use to describe me
2.air_q1: Where do I show up as my best self?
2.air_q2: Where, or with whom, do I slip?
2.air_q3: Under what pressures do I most often slip: tired, scared, rushed, criticized?
beliefs: I am who I am. People don't really change.
Being kind means being a pushover.
If I make a mistake, it proves I'm not a good person.
My worth depends on what other people think of me.
Who I am is built in small, unseen choices.
I can grow at any age, from any starting point.
2.horizon_intro: Picture the person you're becoming. How do you handle conflict? How do you treat people under pressure? What do you do when you get it wrong? What's it like to be around you?
2.horizon_label: Me at my best, living these qualities
2.why_label: Living these qualities matters to me because…
2.wordbank_label: The qualities I choose to live by
flight: where did I live my qualities today, where did I miss, what will I do tomorrow
How I'll repair when I get it wrong
Who helps me see myself clearly
one trusted person who tells me the truth, kindly
2.soul_intro: Each day for seven days, make one small choice that lives out one of your qualities, when no one is watching and no one will ever know. Write the quality and the choice.

3.title: Emotional Life
3.quote: Feelings are information, not instructions. You can't stop the wind, but you can learn to fly with it.
3.care: This program is for reflection and growth. It isn't therapy or a substitute for professional care. If something heavy comes up, reach out to someone you trust or a counselor. In a crisis, contact local emergency services; in the US, call or text 988.
3.air_intro: Your emotions are the air you fly through: lift, headwind, sometimes storm. No judgment here. Every habit you have with feelings made sense at some point.
3.air_words: The three feelings that visit me most often these days
3.air_q1: When a hard feeling shows up, what I usually do is…
3.air_q2: Is there an old hurt I'm still carrying? (Name it, or just note that it's there.)
3.air_q3: Growing up, which feelings seemed not to be allowed?
beliefs: Strong people don't cry.
If I let myself feel it, I'll fall apart.
Other people are responsible for how I feel.
Anger is always bad.
Feelings are information, not instructions.
Healing isn't linear, and it's allowed to take time.
3.horizon_intro: Not a life without hard feelings: a life where you feel what you feel, understand what it's telling you, and respond instead of react. How do you meet a hard day? Express anger or hurt? How much room is there for joy?
horizon_extra: The weight I'm ready to begin setting down
optional; "not yet" is an honest answer
flight: once or twice a day, name what I'm feeling in one word
pause, three slow breaths, name it, ask what I need
writing, music, prayer, outdoors, talking, creating, crying
the people I'll reach for; healing happens in connection
3.soul_intro: Three times a day, pause for one breath and ask: What am I feeling (one word)? Where do I feel it in my body? What is it asking for? Write one line each day.

4.title: Health & Fitness
4.quote: Your body isn't an ornament, a project, or the enemy. It's the vessel that carries your life.
4.care: This is for reflection and planning, not medical advice. Before changing your exercise, what you eat, or your medications or treatment, talk with your doctor or care team. This week is for every body.
4.air_intro: Health is care: daily, practical, patient care of the vessel you actually have. Fitness is capacity: the strength and energy to live the life in your Charter.
4.air_words: Three words that describe my relationship with my body right now
4.air_q1: What my body has been trying to tell me lately…
4.air_q2: What gets in the way of caring for my body…
air_grid: How I speak to my body
beliefs: My body has let me down.
Health is for people with more time and money than I have.
If I can't do it perfectly, why bother?
Exercise has to hurt to count.
My body deserves care, exactly as it is today.
Small, steady care changes everything.
4.horizon_intro: Thriving for your body, not anyone else's. How do you feel when you wake? What does your energy carry you through? What movement does your body enjoy? How do you rest? How do you speak to your body?
4.horizon_label: My health & fitness thriving, for my body
4.why_label: Caring for my vessel matters to me because…
flight: one or two changes that help me feel well
whatever movement is available to me; start where I am
a bedtime, a wind-down, rest before I crash
doctor, therapist, trainer, caregivers, a friend; the appointment I've put off
4.soul_intro: Each day for seven days: one act of care for your body, and one thank-you to a part of your body for something it did today. Write one line: the care, and the thank-you.
4.gathering: What did your body tell you this week?

5.title: Intellectual Life
5.quote: A butterfly doesn't fly by strength alone. It reads the air. Your mind does that for you.
5.air_intro: Not your IQ or your degrees: your curiosity, what you feed your mind, how well you think, and whether you're still growing. This week is for every kind of mind.
5.air_words: Three words that describe my mind these days
5.air_q1: What I've been curious about lately…
5.air_q2: The inputs that drain my mind…
beliefs: I'm not smart. I was never a school person.
I'm too old to learn that now.
I don't have time to read.
If I'm not good at it right away, I'm not meant to do it.
My mind grows with use, at any age.
Curiosity is a form of courage.
5.horizon_intro: What are you reading? What are you learning, and how does it feel to be a beginner again? Who makes you think? How clear and focused is your mind? What have you created?
horizon_extra: Three things I'd love to learn or explore in the next year
anything at all; it doesn't have to be practical
5.why_label: A growing mind matters to me because…
flight: one thing from my list, and its first step
people, groups, books or communities that stretch me
5.soul_intro: Each day for seven days, notice one thing you wonder about, then give it ten minutes: look it up, read, ask someone. Write the question and what you found.
5.gathering: Which question led you somewhere unexpected?

6.title: Love Relationship
6.quote: A good partner doesn't carry your wings. You fly alongside each other, choosing again and again to stay in the same sky.
6.care: This week is for everyone: partnered, single, divorced, widowed or "it's complicated". If you feel unsafe, afraid or controlled in a relationship, reach out. In the US: National Domestic Violence Hotline 1-800-799-7233, or text START to 88788. In danger now, call 911.
6.air_intro: Clear sight, not judgment. Partnered: look at your relationship as it is. Single: look at how you give and receive love, and the love you're ready for.
6.air_words: Three words that describe my love life right now
6.air_q1: What's going well that I don't want to lose…
6.air_grid_label: Six parts of partnership (optional if single)
beliefs: If it's right, it should just be easy.
I have to lose myself to keep someone.
It's too late for me to find love, or to rebuild it.
Conflict means we're failing.
Love is a choice I make every day.
I deserve to be loved well, and I can learn to love well.
6.horizon_intro: Partnered: your relationship at its best. How you greet each other, handle disagreements, show affection, dream together. Single: what it feels like to be with the love you're ready for.
horizon_extra: What I bring, and the partner I'm becoming
6.why_label: A thriving love life matters to me because…
flight: listening, raising hard things, coming back after conflict
love shown the way it's received; appreciation said out loud
counselor, mentor couple, class, faith community, friends
6.soul_intro: Each day for seven days, notice one specific thing you appreciate about your partner and tell them. Single? Do it with someone you love, and add one thing you appreciate about yourself. Write what you noticed and how they responded.
6.gathering: How did they respond, and how did it change you?

7.title: Parenting
7.quote: Strong enough to hold them while they grow. Open enough to let them fly on their own wings.
7.care: Three ways through this week, choose one or more: raising children (any kind, any age) · influencing young lives · reparenting the child you once were. If this week touches grief around children, be gentle with yourself, take what serves you, and reach out for support.
7.air_intro: How you help young lives grow, including your own younger self. No perfect parents, only present ones. Reparenting? Rate how you treat the child within.
7.air_words: Three words the young people in my life would use to describe me
7.air_q1: The young people in my circle of care are… (reparenting? include you at age ___)
beliefs: I have to be a perfect parent.
My child's choices are a report card on me.
It's too late to repair things with my children.
I don't have children, so this isn't for me.
Repair matters more than perfection.
The child I was still deserves care.
7.horizon_intro: Raising children: your home, how you talk, how you handle hard moments, your relationship when they're grown. Influencing: the presence you are for them. Reparenting: how you speak to and comfort yourself.
7.horizon_label: This part of my life thriving
horizon_extra: What I most want them to carry from me
values, memories, a way of being in the world
7.why_label: This part of my life matters to me because…
flight: the one or two limits that matter most, held with love
what I'll say out loud; how I'll make it right
co-parent, family, friends, group, counselor, mentor
7.soul_intro: Each day for seven days, notice a young person doing something good, especially character (kindness, effort, honesty, courage), and tell them specifically. Reparenting? Catch yourself shining. Write who, what you saw, and what you said.
7.gathering: What did you see when you looked for it?

8.title: Social Life
8.quote: Monarchs don't winter alone. Even the most beautiful wings need company to make it through the cold.
8.care: Introverts welcome: this week is about depth, not a crowded calendar. If you feel lonely right now, that's very common and not a flaw in you. Circles shrink in some seasons, and they can grow again.
8.air_intro: Your friendships, your community, and the people you choose to travel with. No one should have to travel their path alone.
8.air_words: Three words that describe my social life right now
8.air_q1: The people I'd call if everything fell apart…
8.air_q2: Where I feel lonely or left out…
8.air_grid_label: Six parts of my social life
beliefs: I'm too busy for friends right now.
People don't really want me around.
Making friends as an adult is impossible.
I have to be the strong one. I don't need anyone.
It's worth reaching out first.
I can be a good friend and still have boundaries.
8.horizon_intro: Who's around your table? How often do you laugh? Who do you call on a hard day, and who calls you? Where do you belong? How do you contribute to the people and places you love?
horizon_extra: The kind of friend I'm becoming
who I am to the people in my circle
flight: the two or three friendships I'll invest in on purpose
one new connection, or an old friendship to rekindle
a community where I'm known over time, like the Collective
what drains me, and what I'll protect
8.soul_intro: Each day for seven days, reach toward one person on purpose: a thinking-of-you text, a call, an invitation, a thank-you, a check-in, a hello to someone new. Write who, and what happened.
8.gathering: Who reached back, and what surprised you?

9.title: Financial Life
9.quote: Money is fuel for the flight: not a measure of your worth, and not the point of your life.
9.care: This is for reflection and planning. It isn't financial, legal or tax advice. For decisions about investments, debt, taxes or benefits, talk with a qualified professional. If money stress feels overwhelming, a nonprofit credit counselor is a good first call.
9.air_intro: Look without shame. Shame keeps us from looking, and we can't change what we won't look at. Thriving here means enough, clarity and peace.
9.air_words: Three words that describe my relationship with money
9.air_q1: How I feel when I check my balance…
9.air_q2: The money story I grew up with…
9.air_grid_label: Six parts of my financial life
beliefs: I'm just bad with money.
There will never be enough.
Wanting more money makes me greedy.
If I don't look, it isn't real.
Money is a tool that can serve what I love.
I can learn to handle money well, one small step at a time.
9.horizon_intro: A real, grounded picture. How do you feel checking your accounts? What worries are gone? What cushion do you have? What debt is cleared? How do you give? What money talks have become easy?
horizon_extra: What I want my money to make possible
security, freedom, rest, generosity, experiences, legacy
9.why_label: Peace with money matters to me because…
flight: a regular money date: what came in, went out, is coming
a simple plan that sends money toward what matters
one step: start a fund, list debts, choose the first
how I'll give; who helps me with money
9.soul_intro: Each day for seven days, notice one money moment (a purchase, bill, gift, worry, or moment of enough). Write what it was, whether it matched what matters, how it felt, and one thank-you for something that provided for you.
9.gathering: What did your money tell you about what you value?

10.title: Career
10.quote: Your career is the flight. Your calling is the compass that keeps you oriented when the path twists.
10.care: Career means your work and contribution in every form: employed, business owner, caregiver, homemaker, volunteer, student, retired, between jobs, or unable to work. Building a business? Book a complimentary Next Chapter Call: lccommandsuite.com/book/next-chapter-call
10.air_intro: Bigger than a job title: what you give your time, skill and energy to. When work lines up with your calling, even hard days have meaning.
10.air_words: Three words that describe my work life right now
10.air_q1: The parts of my work that light me up…
10.air_grid_label: Six parts of my work life
beliefs: Work is supposed to be hard. Enjoying it is a luxury.
It's too late for me to change direction.
My worth is measured by how productive I am.
I have to choose between meaningful work and paying the bills.
My work can be an expression of who I am.
Every season of work can teach me something.
10.horizon_intro: What are you doing, and for whom? Which strengths are you using? What does a good workday feel like? How much do you work and rest? What are you known for? What do you receive in return?
horizon_extra: The difference I want my work to make
in one life, my community, or the world
10.why_label: Work aligned with my calling matters to me because…
flight: using more of what I'm good at and love doing
one skill, course, credential or experience
hours, rest, and the no's that make my pace sustainable
mentor, manager, coach, network; the next conversation
10.soul_intro: Each workday for seven days, notice one task that gave you lift (energized you) and one that created drag (drained you). Not in paid work? Use whatever you gave your energy to. Write one line: lift, and drag.
10.gathering: What gave you lift, and what created drag?

11.title: Quality of Life
11.quote: Butterflies bask. Rest, warmth and delight aren't a reward after the flight. They're what make the flight possible.
11.care: Next week is Wings Out: Life Vision and your Charter Signing. Gather all eleven of your "My LifeCharter" chapter pages so far and bring them with you.
11.air_intro: How do your days actually feel? Joy doesn't depend on money, travel, mobility or perfect health. Small joys count as much as big adventures.
11.air_words: Three words that describe how my days feel
11.air_q1: An ordinary day in my life right now looks like…
11.air_q2: What steals joy from my days…
11.air_grid_label: Six parts of my quality of life
beliefs: Joy is a reward I have to earn first.
Rest is lazy.
I'll enjoy life once things settle down.
The good things in life need lots of money, or perfect health.
Small joys, noticed, make a big life.
Rest makes flight possible.
11.horizon_intro: Not a vacation: an ideal ordinary day. How do you wake? What do you eat, and with whom? What fills your morning, afternoon, evening? Where's the beauty and laughter? How do you rest?
11.horizon_label: My ideal ordinary day, morning to night
horizon_extra: Experiences I want to have, big and small
a trip, a concert, a garden, a sunrise, one table full of people I love
11.why_label: Days that feel good to live matter to me because…
flight: one small delight built into every day
a true day off, breaks, a protected bedtime, time away
one change: more beautiful, peaceful or accessible
one experience on the calendar to look forward to
11.soul_intro: Each day for seven days, give yourself ten minutes to savor something good with nothing competing for your attention. No phone, no multitasking. Write what you basked in, and how it felt.
11.gathering: What did you find when you slowed down to savor?

12.title: Life Vision
12.quote: You don't need a perfect wing or a windless day. You have enough clarity to see your next right movement, and the courage to extend your wings into it.
12.care: All twelve of your "My LifeCharter" chapter pages, your Charter Statement, and the signing page at the end of this handout.
